answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied: every agent must lock a small, time-vested bond before it can trade, and its past deals are written into a shared harbor ledger anyone can audit. A sybil swarm can spin up a thousand fresh identities, but each one starts with an empty record, like an opal with no history — no counterparty will trust it with real work. Honest agents slowly earn ivory-grade standing through completed jobs, so the cost of faking trust grows with every fake identity while genuine agents keep their earned access.
